security_audit.summary: Most static findings are lexical false positives from minified GSAP, JavaScript template literals, relative asset references, and documentation. Three runtime CDN requests are confirmed, including one external script without integrity protection. The skill also directs a silent remote self-update and accepts unbounded, unescaped storyboard paths. Static review was capped at 400/462 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 62 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The skill silently runs a remote update before use.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update command. Require explicit user approval, pin the package version, and show the source and proposed changes before installation.

remediation.issue: Storyboard and audio paths are not confined or escaped.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve each path, verify it remains under the project root, restrict extensions, and HTML-escape every generated attribute value.

remediation.issue: Templates and assembled output load fonts or scripts from external CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle approved local copies. Otherwise pin versions, add integrity hashes, document network access, and provide an offline fallback.

remediation.issue: Temporary decoded audio is removed only after successful processing.
remediation.suggestion: Delete the temporary WAV in a finally block so failed ffmpeg or audio parsing cannot leave user media in temporary storage.

content.value_statement: Music videos require precise timing and consistent motion planning. This skill analyzes a track, builds an approved storyboard, assembles frames, verifies playback, and renders an MP4.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes audio with a bundled Python beat-grid script and produces a deterministic timing map.
Plans one to six frames around beats, phrases, energy changes, onsets, rolls, and silences.
Stages optional user images and videos for beat-cut or phrase-paced treatments.
Validates storyboard timing, required frame groups, template references, and total duration.
Assembles frame compositions with background music into a standalone HyperFrames project.
Runs lint, browser validation, frame inspection, approval checkpoints, and MP4 rendering.
limitations: Audio analysis requires Python, librosa, NumPy, SoundFile, ffmpeg, and ffprobe.
Rendering requires the HyperFrames CLI and a browser-capable local environment.
Calm or weakly rhythmic music may require phrase pacing because detected beats can be unreliable.
Some templates load fonts or JavaScript from external CDNs unless those assets are bundled locally.

use_cases.description: Create a validated storyboard and reusable frame compositions before final rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Music Promo
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 15-second beat-synced promo from [audio path]. Use kinetic typography, landscape format, and show the storyboard before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner project with one audio file and no visual assets.

prompt_templates.title: Portrait Image Slideshow
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [audio path] and images from [folder] into a portrait slideshow. Cut on strong beats and use phrase pacing where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Timed Lyric Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lyric video from [audio path] using [lyrics]. Align lines to vocal timing, validate every frame, and provide a contact sheet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Music release with lyrics and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Branded Campaign Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a square campaign video from [audio path]. Use [brand preset], three frame treatments, supplied assets, and render only after approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced branded edit with multiple treatments and strict approval.

output_examples.input: A 30-second synthwave track with no visual assets.
output_examples.output: A 1920x1080 kinetic typography video with three beat-aligned frames, an approved storyboard, validation results, a contact sheet, and an MP4.

output_examples.input: A portrait campaign brief, one song, and six product images.
output_examples.output: A 1080x1920 promotional slideshow with images cut to strong beats, phrase-paced holds, consistent branding, and a rendered video.

output_examples.input: A vocal track and complete lyrics.
output_examples.output: A lyric video plan with timed lines, readable holds, synchronized visual changes, browser verification, and final render details.

best_practices: Use one canonical timing map and keep every frame boundary aligned with its anchors.
Review the storyboard before frame construction and review the assembled video before rendering.
Keep fonts, colors, aspect ratio, duration, and asset paths consistent across all frames.
anti_patterns: Do not estimate beats again by ear or with a second analyzer.
Do not hard-cut calm music to an unreliable beat grid.
Do not render before plan validation, browser checks, frame inspection, and user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill work without images or video clips?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build a complete video with typography, templates, motion primitives, and generated backgrounds.

faq.question: Can it create lyric videos?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide lyrics or use a transcription workflow to obtain word or line timing.

faq.question: Which video formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports landscape, portrait, and square canvases with project-defined dimensions and frame rates.

faq.question: Does it generate music?
faq.answer: It can request a music generation workflow when no track is supplied. Availability depends on configured tools and credentials.

faq.question: What software dependencies are required?
faq.answer: Audio analysis needs Python audio libraries and ffmpeg. Assembly and rendering need Node.js, HyperFrames, and browser validation support.

faq.question: Does the workflow require approval?
faq.answer: Yes. The normal workflow asks for storyboard approval and final render approval. Autonomous mode changes how these checkpoints proceed.
